name: Lyo.Health
tagline: Contract for services that report their own health. Implement `IHealth`. There is no central health service.
description: Contract for services that report their own health. Implement `IHealth`. There is no central health service. A check returns `HealthResult` with status, timings, and optional metadata.

sections.title: The contract
sections.body:
- Hosts label probe output with `HealthCheckName`, a short identifier, for example `"filestorage"`, `"cache"`, `"rabbitmq"`, `"audit-postgres"`, `"change-tracker-postgres"`.
- The live probe is `CheckHealthAsync`. Keep it cheap and short-circuiting, and honor the supplied `CancellationToken`.

sections.title: `HealthResult`
rows: UTC instant the probe finished (set by the factory helpers).
Optional human-readable summary; filled with the exception message on failure.
Schema, version, connection info, key-id, and similar.

sections.title: How to use it
sections.text: Ask the service for health directly. Service interfaces (`IFileStorageService`, `ICacheService`, `IMqService`) extend `IHealth`. Health comes from the service. No separate registration. Hosts that want an aggregate view typically resolve `IEnumerable<IHealth>` and fan out `CheckHealthAsync` in parallel, then publish the resulting `HealthResult` collection.
